headword: {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}

definitions.gloss: welcome and farewell party; combined send-off and welcome party
definitions.explanation: A single gathering that both sends off members who are leaving and welcomes those who are arriving. Common in Japanese workplaces and schools in spring, when transfers and new appointments take effect at once.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}、{歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}がある。
examples.english: There's a welcome and farewell party next week.

examples.japanese: {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}の{幹事|かんじ}を{任|まか}された。
examples.english: I was put in charge of organizing the welcome and farewell party.

examples.japanese: {四月|しがつ}は{異動|いどう}が{多|おお}いので、どの{部署|ぶしょ}でも{歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}が{開|ひら}かれる。
examples.english: There are many transfers in April, so welcome and farewell parties are held in every department.

notes:
{歓送|かんそう} (seeing off) + {歓迎|かんげい} (welcome) + {会|かい} (gathering) — the two words share the {歓|かん} and are combined into one.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}を{開|ひら}く: to hold a welcome and farewell party
- {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}の{幹事|かんじ}: the organizer of the party
- {歓送迎会|かんそうげいかい}に{出席|しゅっせき}する: to attend the party

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
The Japanese fiscal and school year begins in April, so departures and arrivals happen at the same time. Rather than hold two events, workplaces combine them: departing members give a short speech first, then new members introduce themselves.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歓迎会|かんげいかい}: welcome party — for new members only
- {送別会|そうべつかい}: farewell party — for departing members only
